rationale: The pain is real and well-documented: HN threads, Reddit communities, and web performance forums repeatedly surface founder and visitor frustration with bloated, janky AI-generated marketing sites. At least one willingness-to-pay signal exists via the established web performance audit market (competitors charge $99–$500+ per audit or $99–$299/month for automated monitoring). The target buyer — founders who paid to vibe-code a site and now need it to convert — is nameable and reachable. Severity is moderate (not burning) because most founders tolerate poor performance until a conversion drop is noticed, but the frequency of new AI-generated sites shipping with these issues is growing weekly.
